newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on small sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on small sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended 1996 somnolent, with the Tuesday close a shade down from New York's Monday close as trade slowed to a trickle, gold dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$369.10/60 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$369.25/75 close on Monday.
The market saw small amounts of professional sales, but activity was minimal, dealers said.
"We're just providing customer services, no trade is really going on," said one bullion dealer.
Some traders expected gold prices to dip immediately after the market reopened following the holiday season, followed by a gradual correction over the first quarter of 1997.
"I think there will be more position selling after the holidays," said one gold dealer with an international bullion firm.
The Hong Kong gold market will be closed on Wednesday and reopen on Thursday.
After the holidays, gold was likely to stay within a range of $362-370 per ounce, with selling pressure emerging at $370, bullion dealers said.
"If gold breaks through $370 (next quarter) we could see it go to $373 per ounce or so," one gold trader said.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,409 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.00 from its previous fix at -4.00.
